scope.current_boundary: Derive, using W = Fs, the formula \Delta E_P = mg\Delta h for gravitational potential energy changes in a uniform gravitational field, and recall and use the formula in calculations and applications. Emphasize the uniform field condition and path independence. Do not pre-teach kinetic energy derivation (owned by l06) or strain/elastic potential energy (Topic 6).

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Archetypal direct calculation of height h from gravitational potential energy decrease Delta E_P = mg Delta h.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Calculate height of balcony from potential energy decrease of 60 J and mass 0.18 kg.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Requires correct rearrangement of Delta E_P = mg Delta h for height Delta h = Delta E_P / (mg).
lesson_sections_informed: Worked Example 1: Lifting an Industrial Load with a Crane

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Directly tests path independence: gravitational potential energy change depends only on net vertical displacement, not on horizontal or intermediate motion.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Determine gain in potential energy for an object moved down then up along an angled path.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Distractors add all path lengths or confuse horizontal displacement with vertical height.
lesson_sections_informed: Path Independence: Why Only Vertical Height Matters
Worked Example 3: Multi-Stage Path and Path Independence
Check 1: Comparing Paths Up a Cliff

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Requires determining vertical height from distance along an inclined path using trigonometry before calculating Delta E_P = mg Delta h.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Determine decrease in gravitational potential energy for glider descending at 24 degrees to horizontal.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Crucial distinction between distance travelled along path and vertical height difference.
lesson_sections_informed: Path Independence: Why Only Vertical Height Matters
